prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (max. 500 words)

Health and social care
- NHS: Additional revenue funding rising from £8bn in year one to £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years; reduce waiting lists; rapid GP access (same-day for urgent need); universal NHS dentistry access; new dentistry contract; dentistry funding rising to £3bn/yr by 2030; restore public health budgets (+£1.5bn).
- Primary care: Funding +£1.5bn/yr by 2030; £2bn capital; expand community diagnostics.
- Workforce: Budget uplift to settle NHS pay; junior doctor pay restoration.
- Cancer: National plan to hit 75% early diagnosis by 2028; public health prevention; publicly funded research.
- Mental health: Evidence-based therapies within 28 days; school/college counsellors; tailored services; support for neurodivergent children.
- Assisted dying: Support change with safeguards.
- HIV: End new transmissions by 2030 via PrEP and expanded opt-out testing.

Social care and disability
- Free personal care; £20bn/yr investment; national career/pay framework for care workers; visa reform to prevent exploitation; legal right to an essential care supporter.
- Disability: +5% to disability benefits; oppose PIP voucher replacement; reform assessments; free transport for 16–18 SEND; support inclusive design; workplace support.
- Children’s social care: +£3bn to councils; guaranteed counselling; extend “staying put” to 21.

Housing and planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes/yr; end Right to Buy; local rent controls; end Section 21; long-term leases; tenant right to energy upgrades; local tenancy boards; first-refusal powers for councils/RSLs on specified properties; bring empty homes into use.
- Retrofit and standards: £29bn home insulation to EPC B; £9bn low‑carbon heat; £4bn for public buildings; £7bn heat adaptation; LA-led street/area programmes; property-linked finance; new homes to Passivhaus-equivalent with solar/low‑carbon heat; raise PRS minimum to EPC C; whole-life carbon in planning; mandate reuse of demolition materials.

Energy and climate
- No new oil/gas licences; end fossil subsidies; carbon tax starting £120/t, rising to up to £500/t within 10 years.
- Renewables: Wind ~70% of electricity by 2030; targets by 2035 of 80GW offshore, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar; end barriers to onshore wind; support community energy; Crown Estate into public ownership (Welsh assets devolved).
- Grid/storage: Major grid expansion; offshore networks; more interconnectors; rapid storage scale-up; green hydrogen for industry.
- Nuclear: Stop new projects; phase out existing.

Economy, taxation, and public ownership
- Public investment averaging £40bn/yr (rail electrification and reopenings; building retrofit; storage; water/sewage; active travel; industry decarbonisation; public transport).
- Public ownership: Rail, water companies, and Big 5 retail energy suppliers.
- Finance: BoE mandate to support transition; credit guidance; banks/NBFIs to exit fossil assets by 2030; FCA to eliminate new fossil listings.
- SMEs: Regional mutual banks (capitalised incl. £10bn public); £2bn/yr grants for decarbonisation; prompt payment law.
- Tax: Wealth tax 1% >£10m and 2% >£1bn; align CGT and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper limit; reform IHT; revalue Council Tax; remove selected business rate reliefs; higher windfall taxes; VAT cuts for hospitality/arts, rises for private education/financial services; carbon tax revenues up to ~£80bn/yr by end of parliament; enhanced HMRC enforcement. Borrow to invest.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature Act; 30% land/sea protected by 2030; Clean Air Act; DEFRA +£1.5bn; public ownership of water; end sewage discharges via enforcement; Right to Roam; peat rewetting; woodland/scrub/urban biodiversity measures; 30% fully protected MPAs; ban destructive fishing in MPAs.
- Animal protection commission; ban blood sports; end badger cull; phase out factory farming practices (cages, routine antibiotics); ban snares/lead ammo; tighter breeding/import rules; long-term move away from animal testing.
- Farming: Nearly triple support to farmers for nature-friendly practices; expand horticulture; link payments to pesticide reduction; strengthen food security; universal free school meals and breakfast clubs to Year 6; food education; local food partnerships; cut waste.

Education
- End high-stakes primary/secondary testing; abolish Ofsted; inclusive SEND support (+£5bn); free school meals; restore school nurses and counsellors.
- Early years: £1.4bn/yr for Sure Start; extend childcare to 35 hours/week from 9 months.
- Schools: +£8bn incl. £2bn teacher pay; £2.5bn/yr for RAAC/safety; curriculum balance incl. climate/Natural History GCSE; bring academies under LAs; VAT on private schools (SEN exempt); retain RSHE.
- Post-16/FE: +£3bn sixth forms; £12bn FE/skills; restore EMA. HE: scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; address TPS.

Transport
- Public transport subsidies to £10bn/yr; free buses for under‑18s; £19bn over five years for public transport/electrification/active travel; rail back to public ownership; local bus control; £2.5bn/yr for cycling/walking.
- Roads: Oppose new roads; restore fuel duty escalator; road pricing; EV scrappage up to £5bn/yr; end new ICE sales by 2027 and ICE road use by 2035; VED by vehicle weight; 20mph default in built-up areas; shift freight to rail.
- Aviation: Frequent-flyer levy; ban domestic flights where rail <3h; carbon tax on kerosene; no airport expansion; worker transition.

Democracy, rights, migration
- Fair Politics Act: repeal voter ID; proportional representation; state party funding; transparency on lobbying/think tanks; strengthen Electoral Commission; votes from 16; amend Online Safety Act for election integrity. Replace House of Lords with elected chamber; constitutional review; devolve further; +£5bn/yr to English local government; defend HRA/ECHR; restore legal aid; repeal restrictive protest laws; support gender recognition reform.
- Migration/asylum: End hostile environment, NRPF, and 10‑year route; safe routes; allow work while awaiting decisions; fast/fair processing; split Home Office functions; simplify/at‑cost visas; free NHS for visa holders; remove spousal income thresholds; voting rights for visa holders.

Justice and drugs
- End routine stop-and-search and facial recognition; diversity fitness assessments; stronger local scrutiny.
- Presumption against custodial sentences under two years; expand diversion/restorative justice.
- VAWG strategy; misogyny as hate crime; fund services; decriminalise sex work.
- Courts: +£11bn over parliament; more judges; repair courts.
- Drugs: National Commission; decriminalise personal possession; harm-reduction approach.

Foreign policy and Europe
- Uphold international law; support Ukraine; aim to rejoin EU (customs union first), restore free movement and Erasmus.
- Israel/Palestine: Immediate ceasefire; recognise Palestine; end UK arms exports to Israel; pursue war crimes accountability.
- Aid/climate finance: ODA to 1% GNI and climate finance to 1.5% by 2033; Loss and Damage contributions; debt relief; ecocide law.
- Nuclear/NATO: Sign TPNW; cancel Trident; pursue NATO reforms incl. No First Use.
